newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hostage rescue victims recovering-Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostage rescue victims recovering-Fujimori.

text.p: Victims from the dramatic commando hostage-rescue operation at the Japanese ambassador's residence were recovering well in a military hospital, President Alberto Fujimori said on Wednesday.

Many of the injured hostages suffered bullet wounds as they crawled out of the besieged diplomatic mansion in the middle of a fierce gunbattle between the rescuers and their heavily-armed Marxist rebel captors.

Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, who suffered a leg wound, was "well on the way to recovery," Fujimori said at a press conference in the presidential palace at which he gave a blow-by-blow account of the assault.
Another victim, Luis Serpa, underwent an operation on his upper colon and has bullet fragments in his liver, he said.
Fujimori personally ordered the attack on the residence where 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary rebels held 72 hostages for 126 days to demand the release of their jailed comrades.
All the guerrillas were killed in the attack, along with one captive, judge Carlos Giusti, and two of the commandos.
Fujimori said Giusti bled to death after being being shot in the crossfire. Earlier reports said he suffered a heart attack after being shot.
The remarkably low death toll was due partly to the fact that security forces gave the hostages some prior warning of the attack so they didn't panic, Fujimori said.
He didn't say how they were told but military sources said it was via a pager which one of the captives had managed to hold onto during the siege.
